chapters.title: Getting started
intro: This chapter is for everyone who uses the SupportDesk desk: agents, supervisors and administrators.
It shows how to join your team, sign in and find your way around. It also covers your profile, your password, two-step verification and signing out.

sections.title: What you need to sign in
intro: You sign in to the desk with three details. Your administrator gives them to you.
Customers do not use the desk. They use the customer portal, which has its own sign-in.

rows: Your company's SupportDesk name, for example `acme`. Every company has its own workspace.
The e-mail address your administrator used when they added you.
The password you chose when you accepted your invitation.

blocks.note: If you are new, you first get an invitation e-mail. Accept it to choose your password. See [Accept an invitation](#gs-accept-invitation).

sections.title: Accept an invitation
sections.intro: When an administrator adds you as an agent, SupportDesk sends you an invitation e-mail. Use it to choose your password.
prerequisites: You have the invitation e-mail. It contains a link and an invitation code.

steps.text: Open the link in the invitation e-mail.
steps.note: The **Join your team** page opens. **Workspace** and **Work e-mail** are often filled in for you.

steps: Check the **Workspace** and **Work e-mail** fields.
In **Invitation code**, enter the code from the e-mail. It looks like `K7QM-4ZP2`.
If your name is wrong, enter it in **Your name**. Leave it empty to keep the name your administrator entered.
In **New password**, enter a password. Use at least 10 characters with upper-case and lower-case letters and a digit.
In **Confirm password**, enter the same password again.

steps.caption: The **Join your team** page with the invitation code filled in.
steps.alt: Join your team form with workspace, work e-mail, invitation code, name and password fields

sections.result: The page says **You're all set**. Select **Go to sign in** to sign in for the first time.

blocks.note: Your organisation may ask for longer or stronger passwords. **Set password** stays unavailable until both password fields match.

sections.title: Sign in to the desk
sections.intro: Sign in at the start of each working day, or when your session has ended.
prerequisites: You know your workspace name, work e-mail and password.
steps: Open the desk address that your administrator gave you. The **Sign in to SupportDesk** page opens.
In **Workspace**, enter your workspace name.
In **Work e-mail**, enter your work e-mail address.
In **Password**, enter your password.

steps.text: To check what you typed, select the eye button at the end of the **Password** field.
steps.note: The button shows or hides your password. Hide it again if someone can see your screen.

steps: Select **Sign in**.
sections.result: The desk opens on the first module you can use, usually **Command Center**. If two-step verification is on, the **Two-step verification** page opens first.

blocks.caption: The sign-in page with the workspace and work e-mail filled in.
blocks.alt: Sign in to SupportDesk page with numbered highlights on the fields, the eye button, the Sign in button and the theme button

callouts: **Workspace**: your company's SupportDesk name.
**Work e-mail**: the address you were invited with.
**Password**: your desk password.
The eye button shows or hides the password.
**Sign in** checks your details and opens the desk.
The moon or sun button switches between light and dark theme.

blocks.note: The page remembers your workspace and e-mail on this device. It never stores your password.

blocks.tip: If you open a desk link while signed out, the desk takes you to that page after you sign in.

blocks.caption: If a field is empty or wrong, a message appears under it.
blocks.alt: Sign in form with the messages Enter your workspace name, Enter a valid e-mail address and Enter your password

sections.title: Enter a two-step verification code
sections.intro: Two-step verification adds a code to your password. You need it when you turned it on, or when your workspace requires it.
prerequisites: You entered your workspace, e-mail and password, and selected **Sign in**.
steps: Wait for the **Two-step verification** page to open.

steps.text: If you see two buttons, choose **E-mail code** or **Authenticator app**.
steps.note: **Authenticator app** is chosen for you when you have set one up.

steps: Find the 6-digit code in the e-mail from SupportDesk, or in your authenticator app.
In **Verification code**, enter the code.

steps.caption: The **Two-step verification** page for an e-mailed code.
steps.alt: Two-step verification page with the verification code field, the Verify button and the Use a different account button

callouts: **Verification code**: enter the code from the e-mail or the app.
**Verify** checks the code and opens the desk.
**Use a different account** takes you back to the sign-in page.

blocks.note: In a demo workspace, a box on this page shows the code for you. Real workspaces never show it.

blocks.tip: Codes expire after a short time. If a code fails, get a new one and try again.

sections.title: Forgotten passwords, expired passwords and ended sessions
intro: The desk has no self-service password reset. If you forget your password, ask your SupportDesk administrator to reset it.

Your workspace may make passwords expire. When yours has expired, the **Password expired** page opens after you sign in. Ask your administrator to reset your password. Then select **Back to sign in** and sign in again.

blocks.caption: The sign-in page after a session has ended.
blocks.alt: Sign in page with the message Your session ended. Please sign in again.

blocks: Sessions end after a time set by your administrator. They also end when an administrator signs you out. The sign-in page then shows **Your session ended.** and asks you to sign in again.
The desk sign-in page has no single sign-on button yet. Sign in with your workspace, e-mail and password.

blocks.heading: Other links on the sign-in page

list: **Start a free trial** creates a new workspace. See the chapter about subscription, billing and the free trial.
**Platform console** is for the people who run the SupportDesk service. See the chapter about the platform console.

sections.title: The desk screen
sections.intro: Every desk page has the same frame. The navigation rail is on the left. The top bar is above the page.

blocks.caption: The desk with the navigation rail and the top bar highlighted.
blocks.alt: Desk screen with numbered highlights on the navigation rail, Collapse, search box, New ticket, bell, availability, theme button and account menu

callouts: The navigation rail lists the modules you can open, grouped under **Work**, **Customers**, **Operations** and **Settings**.
**Collapse** shrinks the rail to icons only.
The search box opens the command palette.
**New ticket** creates a ticket. You see it only if your role lets you create tickets.
The bell shows your notifications and the number of unread ones.
Your availability, such as **Online**. Select it to change it.
The theme button switches between light and dark theme.
Your avatar opens the account menu.

blocks: You see only the modules your role allows. If a module is missing, ask your administrator for access.
When the connection drops, a bar says **Live updates paused — reconnecting…**. The desk keeps working. Lists catch up when the connection returns.

blocks.tip: On a phone, the rail is hidden. Select the menu button at the top left to open it.

sections.title: Modules in the navigation rail
sections.intro: This table lists every module. The keys are the shortcut that opens the module.

rows: Your live queue, SLA risk and team activity at a glance.
Saved views, the ticket list and the ticket workbench.
Live chat, social and messaging conversations.
Accounts, contacts, locations and their support history.
Products, modules, versions, installations, assets and contracts.
Departments, teams, skills, shifts and agent availability.
SLA policies, business hours, holidays and live breach risk.
Assignment rules, workflows, macros, escalations and schedules.
Articles, categories, review and portal publishing.
Dashboards, reports, scheduled exports and drill-downs.
Summaries, reply drafts, triage suggestions and approved AI actions.
The engineering board: escalated defects, fix versions and releases.
Users, roles, channels, ticket configuration, security and audit.

sections.title: Collapse or expand the navigation rail
sections.intro: Collapse the rail to give the page more room.
steps: At the bottom of the navigation rail, select **Collapse**.

steps.text: To see the name of a module, point to its icon.
steps.caption: The collapsed rail shows icons only.
steps.alt: Narrow navigation rail with module icons and an expand button at the bottom

steps: To show the labels again, select the expand button at the bottom of the rail.
sections.result: The rail shows icons only, or icons with labels. The desk remembers your choice on this device.

sections.title: Run a command from the command palette
sections.intro: The command palette lets you go anywhere and do common jobs without the mouse.

steps.text: Press [[Ctrl+K]], or [[⌘+K]] on a Mac. You can also press [[/]] or select the search box in the top bar.
steps.caption: The command palette before you type.
steps.alt: Command palette listing Navigation commands with their shortcut keys

steps: Type part of what you want, such as `analytics` or `password`.
Press [[↑]] or [[↓]] to choose a result.
Press [[Enter]] to run it, or select it with the mouse.
sections.result: The palette closes and runs the command. To close it without running anything, press [[Esc]].

blocks.heading: What you can do from the palette

list: Go to any module you can open.
Set your availability, for example **Set availability: Away**.
Switch the theme with **Toggle light / dark theme**.
Find a ticket. See [Find a ticket from the command palette](#gs-find-ticket).

blocks: On the **Tickets** screen, the palette also offers commands for the open ticket. The ticket chapters describe them.

blocks.note: When the search box is empty, a **Recent** group lists the last five commands you ran.

sections.title: Find a ticket from the command palette
sections.intro: Open a ticket by its number, or search tickets by text.
steps: Press [[Ctrl+K]] to open the command palette.
Enter the ticket number, such as `#1042` or `1042`. Or enter at least two characters of text.

steps.text: Wait for the **Tickets** group to appear.
steps.caption: Search results for `report` in the command palette.
steps.alt: Command palette with a Tickets group listing six tickets and their statuses, and a Commands group below

steps: Select the ticket you want.

blocks.note: Text search shows up to six tickets, newest activity first. The palette does not search customers yet. Use the **Customers** module instead.

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts
sections.intro: Press [[?]] on any page to see the shortcuts that work there. You can also open the account menu and select **Keyboard shortcuts**.

blocks.caption: The **Keyboard shortcuts** dialog on the Command Center.
blocks.alt: Keyboard shortcuts dialog with General, Navigation and Actions groups

rows: Open or close the command palette.
Everywhere, even while you type in a field.
Open search, that is, the command palette.
Switch between light and dark theme.
Go to a module. See [Modules in the navigation rail](#gs-modules).
If you can open that module.

blocks: For two-key shortcuts, press the second key within about one second.
Single-key shortcuts do nothing while you type in a field. Press [[Esc]] or select an empty part of the page first.

blocks.note: The **Tickets** screen adds its own shortcuts, such as moving through the list and replying. The dialog lists them while you are on that screen.

sections.title: Set your availability
sections.intro: Your availability tells routing and your team whether you can take new work.
steps: In the top bar, select your availability, such as **Online**.

steps.caption: The availability menu. A tick marks your current status.
steps.alt: Availability menu with Online, Away, Busy and Offline and a short hint under each

sections.result: The coloured dot and the label in the top bar change. Your avatar shows the same colour.

blocks.note: Your shifts and idle time do not change your availability. Set it yourself when you start, pause or stop work.

blocks.tip: You can also open the command palette and run **Set availability: Away**, or another status.

sections.title: Switch between light and dark theme
sections.intro: The desk follows your computer's light or dark setting at first. You can choose your own.
steps: In the top bar, select the moon button for dark theme, or the sun button for light theme.
To switch back, select the button again, or press [[Shift+T]].
sections.result: The desk changes theme at once. After you switch, it no longer follows your computer's setting.

blocks.tip: The sign-in page has the same button at the top right.

sections.title: The account menu
sections.intro: Select your avatar at the top right to open the account menu. It shows your name, e-mail and workspace.

blocks.caption: The account menu.
blocks.alt: Account menu with the user's name, e-mail and workspace, and the items My profile, Change password, Two-factor authentication, Keyboard shortcuts and Sign out

rows: Opens your profile. See [Update your profile](#gs-profile).
Opens the **Password** tab. See [Change your password](#gs-change-password).
Opens the **Two-factor** tab. The hint shows **On** or **Off**.

sections.title: Update your profile
sections.intro: Your profile holds your name, time zone, language and e-mail signature.
steps: Select your avatar, then select **My profile**. You can also press [[G]] then [[M]].
On the **Profile** tab, check or change **Display name**.
In **Time zone**, choose your time zone. Dates and SLA times use this zone.
In **Language & format**, choose how dates and numbers look.
In **E-mail signature**, write the text that ends your e-mail replies.
Select **Save profile**.

blocks.caption: The **Profile** tab of **My profile**.
blocks.alt: My profile page with numbered highlights on the tabs, identity card, display name, time zone, language, e-mail signature and Save profile

callouts: The tabs: **Profile**, **Password** and **Two-factor**.
Your name, e-mail and workspace, your user type and your departments. A **Light agent** badge shows if you are one.
**Display name**: the name colleagues and customers see.
**Time zone**: used for dates and SLA times.
**Language & format**: how dates and numbers look.
**E-mail signature**: added to your outgoing e-mail replies.
**Save profile** saves your changes.

blocks.note: SupportDesk adds the signature when it sends an e-mail reply. You do not see it in the reply editor.

sections.title: Change your password
sections.intro: Change your password at any time, for example if you think someone else knows it.
steps: Select your avatar, then select **Change password**. The **Password** tab opens.
In **Current password**, enter the password you use now.
In **New password**, enter a new password of at least 12 characters.
In **Confirm new password**, enter the new password again.

steps.caption: The **Change password** form.
steps.alt: Change password form with current, new and confirm password fields

sections.result: A **Password changed** message appears. Use the new password the next time you sign in.

blocks.tip: A passphrase of several words is easy to remember and hard to guess.

blocks.caption: The form shows a message under each field that needs a fix.
blocks.alt: Change password form with the messages Enter your current password, Use at least 12 characters and The passwords do not match

sections.title: Turn on two-factor authentication
sections.intro: Two-factor authentication protects your account with a code from an authenticator app. You need the app on your phone first.
prerequisites: An authenticator app on your phone, such as Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or 1Password.
steps: Select your avatar, then select **Two-factor authentication**.

steps.caption: The **Two-factor** tab while two-factor authentication is off.
steps.alt: Two-factor authentication card with status Off and the Set up two-factor button

steps: In your authenticator app, scan the QR code that appears.
If you cannot scan it, enter the key shown under **Can't scan? Enter this key manually** in the app instead.
In **Verification code**, enter the 6-digit code the app shows.
Select **Turn on**.
sections.result: A **Two-factor authentication is on** message appears. **Status** shows **On**. From now on, the sign-in asks for a code from the app.

blocks.note: Finish the setup within 15 minutes. After that, select **Set up two-factor** again to get a new QR code.

blocks.tip: To stop without turning it on, select **Cancel**.

sections.title: Turn off two-factor authentication
sections.intro: Turn it off only if you lose your phone or move to another app. You can set it up again at once.
prerequisites: Two-factor authentication is on for your account.

steps.text: Select your avatar, then select **Two-factor authentication**.
steps.caption: The **Two-factor** tab while two-factor authentication is on.
steps.alt: Two-factor authentication card with status On and the Turn off two-factor button

steps: Select **Turn off two-factor**. The **Turn off two-factor authentication?** dialog opens.
Select **Turn off**.
sections.result: A **Two-factor authentication is off** message appears. Your password alone now protects your account.

blocks.warning: Without two-factor authentication, anyone who learns your password can sign in as you.

blocks.note: If your workspace requires two-step verification, the sign-in still asks for a code. The code then comes by e-mail.

sections.title: Sign out
sections.intro: Sign out when you finish work, and always on a shared computer.
steps: Select your avatar at the top right.
Select **Sign out**.
sections.result: The sign-in page opens. Your session on this device has ended.

blocks.tip: You can also open the command palette and run **Sign out**.

sections.title: When a page is missing or closed to you
sections.intro: What you can see depends on your role. Your administrator sets it.

rows: **You don't have access to this area**
Your role lacks the permission for that page.
Select **Go to my workspace**. Ask an administrator if you need the page for your work.
The page does not exist or has moved.
Select **Go to my workspace**, or select **Search** to use the command palette.
**No modules are enabled for your role yet.**
Your role does not open any module.
Ask an administrator for access. You can still open your profile.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **The workspace, e-mail or password is incorrect.**
troubleshooting.cause: One of the three details is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the workspace name, your e-mail and your password. Use the eye button to see what you typed.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **Enter your workspace name.**, **Enter a valid e-mail address.** or **Enter your password.**
troubleshooting.cause: A field is empty, or the e-mail address is not complete.
troubleshooting.fix: Fill in every field, then select **Sign in** again.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says your account is locked and gives a time to try again.
troubleshooting.cause: There were too many failed sign-ins in a row.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait until the time shown, then sign in again. Ask an administrator if you have forgotten your password.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.**
troubleshooting.cause: Too many sign-in attempts came in a short time.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait one minute, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **This workspace is suspended. Contact your administrator.**
The sign-in page says **Cannot reach SupportDesk. Check your connection and try again.**
troubleshooting.fix: Check your network connection, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page refuses your network or asks for single sign-on.
troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace allows sign-in only from certain networks, or requires single sign-on.
troubleshooting.fix: Connect from your office network or company VPN. Otherwise, ask your administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: **Two-step verification** says **That code is not valid or has expired.**
troubleshooting.cause: The code is wrong or too old.
troubleshooting.fix: Get a new code from the e-mail or the app, and enter it at once.

troubleshooting.cause: The code contains letters or spaces.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter only the digits of the code.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Password expired** page opens after you sign in.
troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace makes passwords expire after a set time.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to reset your password. Then select **Back to sign in**.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page shows **Your session ended.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your session timed out, or an administrator signed you out.

troubleshooting.problem: **Change password** says **Use at least 12 characters.** or **The passwords do not match.**
troubleshooting.cause: The new password is too short, or the two new passwords differ.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a new password of 12 characters or more in both fields.

troubleshooting.problem: **Turn on** says **That code did not match. Try the current code.**
troubleshooting.cause: The code from the app was old or mistyped.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the app to show a new code, and enter it at once. Check that your phone's clock is correct.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Time zone** field on **My profile** is empty.
troubleshooting.cause: Your browser lists your time zone under another name, for example **Asia/Calcutta** for India.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose your time zone from the list, then select **Save profile**.

troubleshooting.problem: A **Could not change availability** message appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The change did not reach SupportDesk.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your connection, then choose your availability again.

troubleshooting.problem: A bar says **Live updates paused — reconnecting…**
troubleshooting.cause: The live connection to SupportDesk dropped.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait. The bar disappears when the connection returns. Reload the page if it stays for long.

faq.q: Can I reset my own password if I forget it?
faq.a: Not yet. Ask your SupportDesk administrator to reset it. When you are signed in, you can change your password on **My profile**.

faq.q: Why does a colleague see modules that I do not?
faq.a: Each person sees only the modules their role allows. Ask your administrator if you need another module for your work.

faq.q: Does the desk remember my password?
faq.a: No. The sign-in page remembers only your workspace and e-mail on that device. Your browser may offer to save the password. Do not let it on a shared computer.

faq.q: Can I sign in with my company's single sign-on?
faq.a: Not from the desk sign-in page yet. Sign in with your workspace, e-mail and password.

glossary.definition: Your company's own area in SupportDesk, with its own name, users and data. You enter its name when you sign in.
A sign-in check that asks for a short code after your password. The code comes by e-mail or from an authenticator app. On your profile it is called two-factor authentication.
A phone app, such as Microsoft Authenticator, that shows a new 6-digit sign-in code every few seconds.
A search box that opens with Ctrl+K. It lets you find tickets and run commands from the keyboard.
Your working status: Online, Away, Busy or Offline. Routing uses it to decide who gets new work.
The column on the left of the desk that lists the modules you can open.
The time between signing in and signing out. A session also ends after a set time, or when an administrator ends it.
Text that SupportDesk adds to the end of each e-mail reply you send. You set it on your profile.
